The given relationships connect into a single consistent lineage chain with the following directionality (where ">" denotes an ancestor-to-descendant path of one or more generations):

Mary > Richard > Anna > Christina > Nicholas > Michelle > Gregory > Amber.

This chain is obtained by successive substitution:
- Christina > Nicholas (statement 1) and Nicholas > Michelle (statement 3) together yield Christina > Nicholas > Michelle.
- Michelle > Gregory (statement 2) extends the chain to Christina > Nicholas > Michelle > Gregory.
- Gregory > Amber (statement 5) continues it to Christina > Nicholas > Michelle > Gregory > Amber.
- Anna > Christina (statement 7) prepends Anna, producing Anna > Christina > Nicholas > Michelle > Gregory > Amber.
- Richard > Anna (statement 4) further prepends Richard, producing Richard > Anna > Christina > Nicholas > Michelle > Gregory > Amber.
- Mary > Richard (statement 6) prepends Mary, completing the full chain Mary > Richard > Anna > Christina > Nicholas > Michelle > Gregory > Amber.

Because the chain places Amber after Mary, Amber is a descendant of Mary. This directly matches option 4. The same chain also shows that the two individuals are related by direct ancestry rather than merely sharing an external common ancestor or descendant, eliminating the other options.

Putting it together, Mary is way up there, then Richard, Anna, Christina,Nicholas, Michelle, Gregory, and then Amber below Gregory. So Amber is way down the line from Mary, making Amber Mary's descendant.

Yes, that matches option 4. They do share ancestors, but the precise relationship is that Amber is Mary's descendant.

So, the answer is 4.
